answer: Key the bond to a hardware root of trust and split the signing key across three independent auditors. Measure duplicates by replaying each submission nonce against the ledger, not by comparing names. A sparrow-sized farm that reuses one answer is caught on the second replay. One root per identity means 400 identities need 400 physical boxes, roughly 28,000 dollars before the first payout clears, which closes the tundra of cheap cloud clones and leaves a lotus of virtual machines unable to pass the root check.
